summary: This work demonstrates utility-scale quantum simulation of Markovian dissipative dynamics with collective decay channels on up to 86 emitters (129 total qubits including ancillas) using the IBM Heron processor. The approach combines ancilla-assisted circuit implementations, dynamic circuits with mid-circuit measurements, biased Clifford data regression error mitigation, and Monte Carlo tensor-network validation to reproduce open quantum system evolution beyond classical tractability.
motivation: Simulating open quantum systems with collective dissipation is essential for understanding quantum optics and cavity QED phenomena but remains classically intractable for large systems and challenging on near-term quantum devices due to the need for both local and correlated dissipative channels.
method: Single-qubit and two-qubit dissipators are encoded via ancilla-assisted amplitude damping channels using the interaction basis to decompose collective decay. Hardware-efficient dynamic circuits employing mid-circuit measurements and conditional gates reduce two-qubit depth to constant scaling with system size. Inverse-bias Clifford data regression with biased Cliffordization outperforms zero-noise extrapolation for error mitigation, and a hybrid Monte Carlo time-evolving block decimation algorithm validates results.
result: CDR-corrected quantum experiments on chains of 50 and 86 emitters track Monte Carlo-TEBD classical simulations closely; the largest experiments with $k=3$ Trotter steps contain approximately 8000 two-qubit gates with depth 193, substantially improving upon raw data and capturing superradiant and subradiant dynamics inaccessible to exact simulation.
